Friday, November 21, 2025, 8:28 AM: Our slow-moving third storm has created significant flooding between the 710 interchange and the five freeway heading southbound this morning. The heavy rain produced up to 2 to 4 inches of rain across many locations in addition to the 4 to 12 inches of rain that fell over the past weekend. 

Another storm system is trending for December 1 through the fifth of 2025 that could bring as much rain or more on top of what we just had. This is due to the consistency of the warming of the Pacific that doesn’t seem to stop heating up across the Philippines to the Hawaiian islands. 

Allowing for a parade of storms to slam Southern California, particularly from Santa Barbara to San Diego, but the hardest areas are from Santa Barbara to LA counties even Orange County receives some flooding in Huntington Beach this morning, so no area is unscathed by this atmospheric river and series of storms that continue to strike the region. #CAwx @NWSLosAngeles @realwxforecast @edgarrmcgregor @SoCalweathernet @LaInaMinute

data.raw_text:
In 2025, 470,000 children were evacuated during just ONE typhoon in the Philippines. Schools suspended repeatedly. Education disrupted for months. 

In Europe, children breathed wildfire smoke through summer "holidays." In Jamaica, kids went weeks without power after Melissa. 

These aren't childhood memories of playing outside, they're memories of fleeing for their lives. 48 million children globally have been affected by climate disasters since the first climate summit 30 years ago. We're raising the first generation that sees apocalyptic weather as normal.

What kind of world are we normalizing for children when disaster drills are more common than fire drills? 😨
